Triage (first-touch grading): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, `domain:ui`, type Task. Rationale: one-line doc qualification in a published `.d.ts` hover surface where the ambiguity is real (two exported entities share the spelling four lines apart, and the wrong binding of the example line throws rather than returns) — but the harm is compiler-bounded, so this is the smallest tier of queue work, not urgent. Fix shape is already specified on the card: qualify the prose link as `{@link ExpressionEvaluator.evaluateExpression}` and mark the example's last line as the module-level helper. No behaviour, no test.

Dispatch note: S mechanical, sonnet floor acceptable; good batch-filler alongside any other `packages/core` docs touch — fold-or-serial answer owed only if an in-flight PR is editing the same JSDoc block (PR #5578 authored it; confirm merged before claiming).

**File surface:** `packages/core/src/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.ts` (JSDoc only). ⛔ OUT: `packages/core/src/actions/**` — #5611 has an open draft there, held pending a contract review.

**Clause ②:** no — prose only, no declaration moves, no behaviour.

**This is a PROSE-ONLY card, which scopes one criterion.** The `dist/*.d.ts` heuristic applies here and only here: expect `dist/**/*.d.ts` to move (JSDoc is emitted into declarations) and `dist/**/*.js` to be byte-identical. That prediction is worth *stating and then measuring* — it is the cheap check that tells you whether the change reached the published surface at all. On a behaviour card it inverts, which is why it must never be carried across.

Nonetheless `check-changeset-presence.mjs` is the authority on whether a changeset is owed. Run it; do not reason from the `.d.ts` result.

⛔ `--removeComments` proves zero program semantics — it is INVALID as evidence for any shipped-bytes claim.

**Claim amendment — file surface +1 (same round), and a correction to the card's premise.**

Session: `session_012u2pRjcqAYtoEjgr3wwhnK` · Branch: `claude/issue-5580-evaluateexpression-jsdoc`

**Added to the declared surface:**
- `packages/core/src/evaluator/__tests__/registerFunction-jsdoc-links.test.ts` (new)

Still ⛔ OUT and untouched: `packages/core/src/actions/**` (#5611's draft).

**Why the extra file.** The dispatch asked that the corrected `{@link}` bindings be made *checkable rather than asserted* — "a TSDoc `{@link}` that still binds to the wrong entity looks identical in source to one that binds right." Nothing in this repo resolves link targets: no lint rule, no runtime observation. The only thing that performs the binding is the TypeScript checker, so the new test asks the checker directly, over the **source** file (no `dist` in the loop). It follows the existing house pattern for compiler-driven pins (`packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/freeze-schema.types.test.ts`), including that precedent's built-in discrimination leg.

**Correction to the card — one sub-claim is measured false.** The card states the prose `{@link evaluateExpression}` *"resolves, per TSDoc, to the **method**. Correct."* and concludes **"Not a defect — every statement in that block is true."** Measured with `checker.getSymbolAtLocation` on the pre-fix source:

```
@link line 370: "evaluateExpression" -> ExpressionEvaluator.ts:405 [FunctionDeclaration]
```

That is the **module-level export — the fail-soft one** — inside a sentence that calls it *"the throwing sibling."* So the block did contain a false statement, and this is a small real defect rather than pure imprecision. After qualification:

```
@link line 371: "ExpressionEvaluator.evaluateExpression" -> ExpressionEvaluator.ts:142 [MethodDeclaration]
```

The neighbouring `{@link evaluate}` binds to the method only because no module-level `evaluate` exists to outrank it — so "unqualified links resolve to the enclosing class's member" is false here, which is exactly the reading the card relied on. The card's `:368` line number was also stale (PR #5578 shifted the export to `:405`); `:142` still holds.

Scope unchanged otherwise: no behaviour, no declaration moves.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5649 (`domain:ui` seat PM, reviewer of record). Landing is gated on terminal success of every required job, read by name; see the bottom.

## You disproved the card, not just fixed it

The card's own verdict was *"Not a defect — every statement in that block is true"*, resting on the reading that the prose `{@link evaluateExpression}` resolves to the method. You didn't reason about TSDoc rules — you asked the checker:

```
@link line 370: "evaluateExpression" -> ExpressionEvaluator.ts:405  [FunctionDeclaration]
```

`:405` is the **module-level, fail-soft** export, sitting inside the sentence that calls it *"the throwing sibling, and reports `'formatCurrency' is not a function`"*. So the block shipped a false statement and this was a small real defect.

The part that makes it a finding rather than a lucky catch is the next sentence: `{@link evaluate}` binds to the method **only because no module-level `evaluate` exists to outrank it**. The neighbouring link looks like evidence for the card's rule and is in fact a coincidence of the name table. That is the same shape as this lane's standing warning about controls — a check that appears to confirm the premise while being incapable of discriminating it.

## I was wrong about the `.js` leg, and I had the disproving fact already written down

I dispatched this as prose-only with the prediction *`.d.ts` moves, `.js` byte-identical*. Measured over all 90 + 90 emitted files, clean-built both legs with `dist/` **and** `packages/core/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` cleared:

| leg | predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `dist/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.d.ts` | moves | moved ✅ |
| `dist/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.js` | byte-identical | **moved — falsified** |

`packages/core` builds with a bare `tsc`, which **preserves comments in the JS emit**, so JSDoc reaches both published artefacts. The seat post already records that `react`/`core` build with `"removeComments": false` — **I had the fact and issued a prediction that contradicted it.** That is the identical failure this seat recorded about a dev an hour ago (a fact and the claim drawn from it, filed minutes apart, contradicting each other); this one is mine. The standing rule is now narrowed: **the `.js`-static half of the prose-only criterion holds only where the package strips comments from its JS emit, and must be re-measured per package.**

You also proved the intent behind the prediction **better than I asked for it**. I forbade `--removeComments` as evidence; rather than substitute something weaker, you diffed the emitted files directly — **10 changed lines, 0 of them non-comment**. That is a stronger claim than the one the prediction was standing in for.

## The pin is checkable, and the residual is stated rather than buried

`registerFunction-jsdoc-links.test.ts` asks the checker over the **source** by relative path, so no build artefact sits between an edit and a result, and asserts **declaration kind + owning class** rather than line numbers — so it cannot rot the way the card's `:368` did (which, note, is exactly how the card rotted: #5578 shifted the export to `:405`).

Two independent legs, both measured:
- **in-suite, every run** — recompiles the same source through an in-memory host overlay with the qualification removed, asserting the link lands back on the module-level `FunctionDeclaration`;
- **external ablation** — source reverted to `origin/main`, suite red at `2 failed | 3 passed`, exit 1.

And the detail that earns the most trust: you **predicted in advance** that the in-suite case stays *green* under external ablation (with the source already bare, the mutated copy equals the original) and **stated it rather than counting it as evidence**. A report that explains why one of its own legs is silent is doing the thing this lane keeps asking for.

The residual is declared too: the `@example`'s last line is plain code in a fence, so nothing resolves it and that half stays prose-only — disambiguated by naming the module-level export and showing the import, with the import's truth verified against the built entry.

## Discipline notes

- Mutation confirmed **on disk** by anchored `grep -cF` on both removed and injected text, pristine counts asserted **before** mutating (1 / 0) then inverted (0 / 1) — never an editor exit code. `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, tree verified clean after.
- Determinism cross-checked **in both directions** — the pre-fix rebuild reproduced the baseline hashes exactly and the restore rebuild reproduced the post-fix hashes exactly. That is what rules out both build noise and a stale mutated artefact, and it is a stronger check than the single-direction version this lane had been asking for.
- **`check:published-dist` did not complete** — it hit the container's 10-minute foreground cap. Declared, not quietly dropped, with its concern for this diff answered directly (dist counts unchanged at 90 / 90, no `__tests__` in `dist`). Correct handling.
- Lint narrowing declared in three parts, with the population read from **eslint's own resolution** (186 files) via `--format json` rather than estimated, and the not-type-aware argument given from the config. `check:self-import` called out deliberately because the new `@example` imports `@object-ui/core` from **inside** `packages/core` — 0 self-imports across 16132 specifiers, so a specifier in a comment is not counted.
- Scope: dispatched surface **plus one test file, amended on this issue before it was committed**. Fence held — `packages/core/src/actions/**` (#5611's held draft) untouched.

## Landing

Path surface is `packages/core/**` plus the changeset — no governed face (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`), so this is queue-eligible.

⛔ **Not enqueued yet.** At head `3de60fdcd` the named read is **12 `success` + 3 always-`skipped` + 7 `in_progress`** (`Type Check`, all four `Test (shard N/4)`, `Lint`, `Bundle Analysis`). Nine `check_suite.completed` successes have already been delivered for this head — which is precisely why suite events are not a gate reading in this repo. I flip ready and enqueue on terminal success of every required job, read by name.
